# Juniper Analytics — Incident communication standard

Version 1.0. Effective 1 September 2026.

This standard defines the three supplier obligations reviewed for the named service. Descriptions of internal filing and contacts do not create additional supplier duties. Evidence is assessed as of 17 September 2026; an exception applies only where its conditions are documented.

## 1. Initial notice

The supplier must notify Juniper within 18 hours after becoming aware of an incident affecting Juniper data. An initial notice may be incomplete; notification must not wait for root-cause confirmation.

## 2. Operational updates

For an incident affecting Juniper data, the supplier must send a status update at least once every 12 hours until containment, even when there is no new information.

## 3. Round-the-clock contact

The supplier must maintain a continuously monitored incident contact available to Juniper 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

# Harbor Finch Systems — Service assurance packet

Statement date: 17 September 2026. Scope: the contracted customer service described below.

For incidents affecting this customer, our first external notice is sent 16 hours after root cause is confirmed. Our contractual procedure prohibits any customer notification before that confirmation, even when we are already aware of the incident.

During containment our incident commander publishes status updates; no maximum interval and no handling of periods without new information are specified in this packet.

The customer can call the continuously staffed incident line at any hour, including weekends and holidays; the monitoring team responds around the clock.

### Harbor Finch Systems administrative register 001: capacity planning

Record S03-OP-101 describes the capacity planning workstream for the hosted business service. The service directory associates this workstream with internal team 1 and release cohort 1. A coordinator compares the open work list with the preceding release summary and records items awaiting another team. The directory distinguishes a production service identifier from a training-workspace identifier; labels in screenshots are illustrative and do not expand contractual scope. This entry records 2 unresolved administrative items and 3 closed items, with a reference to meeting note S03-MN-201. Scheduling information supports delivery planning and is not evidence of security approval. The appended worksheet describes ordinary service administration; it makes no statement about backup encryption, customer authorization for data exports or export-record retention. The next register entry covers release scheduling, with separate owners and work references.

# Pinecrest Operations — Service assurance packet

Statement date: 17 September 2026. Scope: the contracted customer service described below.

Schedule A, signed 2 September 2026, requires the first notice of a customer-data incident within 10 hours of awareness, without waiting for root cause. The accompanying statement says this schedule is currently binding for the contracted service.

Schedule B, also signed 2 September 2026, requires the first notice of the same customer-data incident exactly 36 hours after awareness. The accompanying statement says this schedule is currently binding for the same service. Neither schedule specifies precedence or supersedes the other.

Until containment we send a status update every 8 hours, including an explicit no-change update when no new information exists.

The incident contact is staffed only from 09:00 to 17:00 on weekdays. Outside that interval a mailbox stores messages until the next staffed shift.

expected_assessments.rationale: The currently binding schedules prescribe incompatible notice times for the same event; no precedence resolves them.

any_of.quote: Schedule A, signed 2 September 2026, requires the first notice of a customer-data incident within 10 hours of awareness, without waiting for root cause. The accompanying statement says this schedule is currently binding for the contracted service.

Schedule B, also signed 2 September 2026, requires the first notice of the same customer-data incident exactly 36 hours after awareness. The accompanying statement says this schedule is currently binding for the same service. Neither schedule specifies precedence or supersedes the other.

expected_assessments.rationale: Eight-hour updates cover the entire containment period including no-change intervals.

any_of.quote: Until containment we send a status update every 8 hours, including an explicit no-change update when no new information exists.

expected_assessments.rationale: An unmonitored overnight mailbox does not meet continuously monitored 24/7 availability.
